title: Backend channel/Autoenvelope exposure -- non-blocking review follow-ups
description: Non-blocking finding from pr-reviewer's review of PR #146 (backend-channel-envelope-exposure), tracked here per CLAUDE.md's autonomous-pipeline rule so it isn't lost once that PR merges.

checklist.step: app/signals/engine.py's TestAnalyseHistoryPerformance class (backend/tests/unit/signals/test_engine.py) asserts, via a wraps= spy, that ema/macd_components/stochastic_oscillator/force_index are each computed exactly once per analyse_history() call regardless of bar count -- the whole point of the precompute-and-slice pattern PR #146 itself extended to channel_upper/channel_lower (see that task's second decisions entry). PR #146 did not add an analogous spy-based test asserting autoenvelope() is likewise called exactly once (not once per bar) inside analyse_history(); manual inspection of the code confirms the call site is correctly placed outside the per-bar loop (backend/app/signals/engine.py's channel_bands_full = autoenvelope(daily_close, mid=ema_13_full) line, computed once, then sliced via .iloc[:i+1] per bar), so this is a test-coverage symmetry gap, not a live bug -- but a future refactor could silently reintroduce a per-bar autoenvelope() call without any test catching it. Add a mocker.spy/wraps= assertion (assert_count == 1) for autoenvelope, mirroring the existing ema/macd/stochastic/force_index assertions in that same test class.
